RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, the August 5, 2005/Sravana 14, 1927 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests; Food Processing
Industries; Health and Family Welfare; Railways; Steel)

†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Amendment of Indian Forest
Act, 1927
*181. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of  ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
considering  to amend the Indian Forest
Act, 1927;
(b) if so, whether Government have
also decided to pass the Scheduled
Tribes (Recognition of Forest Rights)
Bill;
(c) whether the Forest Conservation
Act, 1980 which expanded IFA's scope by
centralizing State powers over forests made
the prior approval of the Central
Government necessary for dereservation
of reserved forests for use of forest land
for non-forest purposes; and
(d) by what time the Bill is likely to be
introduced and passed?
Anthrax disease
*182. SHRI N.K. PREMA-
CHANDRAN: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether any State in the country is
under Anthrax threat and if so, the details
of cases of Anthrax disease reported so far,
State-wise;
(b) the precautions proposed to be
taken by Government to check the disease;
and
(c) whether any package of assistance
has been made available to the State
Governments under the Centrally
sponsored schemes to control the disease?
Wheat production
†*183. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRI JANARDAN
DWIVEDI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the stock of
wheat during July, 2005 in the country has
come down to around 143 lakh tonnes;

56
(b) if so, the reasons for continuous
decline in the production of wheat;
(c) the steps being taken by
Government for increasing production of
wheat to keep pace with the increase in
population of the country;
(d) the scheme formulated by
Government to increase wheat production
and various other crops so that their
production does not decline in future;
and
(e) whether Government would also ban
residential use of agricultural land to
increase the production of wheat and
various other crops, if not, the reasons
therefor?
Expansion of RINL
*184. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA:
SHRIMATI SUKHBUNS
KAUR:
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Planning
Commission has approved the expansion
plan for Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd. (RINL)
to increase its production from the present
31/2 million tonnes to 7 million tonnes;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government are seriously thinking of
merging RINL with SAIL;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor;
(e) whether any consultations with
State Government and the major political
parties of the State have been held; and
(f) if so, what are Government's views
thereon?
Impact of Patent Laws on pharma
sector
*185. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY:
SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have assessed
the impact of recent Patent Laws on the
restructuring of pharma-sector in the
country;
(b) if not, the reasons therefor;
(c) if so, whether such restructuring
would cause the closure of some units;
(d) if so, what will be the extent of
unemployment due to closure of units; and
(e) what steps are being taken to absorb
the skilled manpower of the closed units?
Streamlining Healthcare system
*186. SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether, in a bid to streamline and
step up healthcare system in the country,
Planning Commission has suggested
measures including setting up a Public
Health Development Authority with a
corpus of Rs. 500 crore and launching
'Sarwa Swasthya Abhiyan' to make
healthcare accessible to all;
(b) if so, whether any concrete measures
have been suggested by them as to how
these healthcare schemes have to be
implemented; and
(c) if so, by when Government are likely
to implement such schemes?

57
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Rent paid to private godowns
by FCI
*187. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS,  FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) the rent paid to private godowns by
the Food Corporation of India in 2004-05
in the country;
(b) the rent expected to be paid by FCI
to private godowns in 2005-06 in the
country;
(c) whether it is a fact that FCI had
entered into agreements with a number of
private godown owners during the last three
years;
(d) whether it is also a fact that no  effort
has been made by FCI to review and ask
the godown owners to reduce their rents
and charges; and
(e) the reasons for this soft approach
towards godown owners who are
profiteering on a huge scale at public
expense?
Two child norm
†*188. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that it is necessary
to follow two child norm in the family to
control the population of the country;
(b) if so, the reaction of Government in
this regard;
(c) whether it is a fact that several State
Governments in the country have taken
steps to follow the above norm; and
(d) if so, the names of the States and the
steps taken by them in this regard?
Privatisation of FCI
*189. SHRI THANGA TAMIL
SELVAN: Will the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have decided to privatise Food Corporation
of India (FCI) through McKinsey and
Company and other private agencies;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what about the service conditions of
FCI employees and the labourers?
Discovery of new species of fresh
water fish
*190. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that four year
study done as a joint project by the
National Agricultural Technology Project
and the Indian Council of Agricultural
Research have discovered eight new species
of fresh water fish;
(b) if so, the names of new species;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the study
has also highlighted the fact that fifty five
species of Kerala's fresh water fish are on
the verge of extinction; and
(d) if so, the action Government
propose to take to save the endangered
species?

58
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Norms for use of pesticides in soft
drinks
†*191. SHRIMATI SAVITA SHARDA :
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
Committee constituted for setting norms
for the use of pesticides in soft drinks has
not taken any decision in this regard, so far;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) by when a decision is likely to be
taken by the Committee in this regard?
Financial assistance to fishermen
*192. SHRI THENNALA G.
BALAKRISHNA PILLAI: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
a number of Indian fishing boats have been
held up in Pakistan;
(b) if so, whether Government have any
scheme to assist such fishing boat owners
through financial assistance;
(c) if so, the details thereof, and if not,
the reasons therefor;
(d) the steps taken to cover such Indian
fishermen through an insurance scheme like
the crop insurance, etc.;
(e) the details of steps taken by the
Central Government to help Indian fishing
sector facing such obstacles;
(f) whether Fisheries Division has  taken
any step to arrange a meeting on this matter;
and
(g) if so, the details thereof?
Authority for disease surveillance
*193. SHRI R.K. ANAND: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that his Ministry
had announced setting up a separate
authority for disease surveillance to monitor
and check the prevalence of communicable,
non-communicable and pollution-related
diseases in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c)  whether it is also a fact that the
Indian Council of Medical Research had an
on-going Rs. 400 crore Integrated Disease
Surveillance Programme; and
(d) the reasons why surveillance and
research should not be carried out by the
same agency?
Efficiency test for medical
practitioners
*194. SHRI PRAMOD MAHAJAN:
SHRI DATTA MEGHE:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are planning to make renewal of Medical
Practitioners (Doctors) mandatory after
specific time intervals;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Increase in drug prices
†*195. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the selling
price of medicines for consumers in the

59
country has increased as a result of
Government taxes, dividend of
manufacturer and commission for
distribution;
(b) if so, the reaction of Government in
this regard; and
(c) the estimated difference between
production cost of medicine and consumer
selling price in the country on an average?
Earnings by Railways
*196. SHRIMATI JAMANA DEVI
BARUPAL:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether in order to project profit
this fiscal without increasing fares, Indian
Railways is aiming at 12 per cent growth in
passenger earnings by reallocating coaches
from trains with low occupancy to those
having high waiting lists;
(b) if so, whether zonal railways have
been empowered to take decision in this
regard by studying occupancy patterns of
different trains operating under them;
(c) whether a new management
information system software has been
devised on the basis of below occupancy
data raised from computerized passenger
reservation system all over the country;
and
(d) whether this has improved the
financial position of Railways?
Antyodaya Anna Yojana
*197. SHRI YASHWANT SINHA: Will
the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of additional households
covered by the Antyodaya Anna Yojana
during the year 2004-2005; and
(b) the break-up of these additional
households, State-wise?
Proposal for new rail lines in
Assam
*198. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether any proposal from Assam
for new railway lines has been received
during 2004-05 and 2005-06;
(b) if so, the action taken thereon;
and
(c) the present status of the above
proposal?
Population control
*199. DR. NARAYAN SINGH
MANAKLAO: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that few States
have crossed the benchmark of population
growth by registering Total Fertility Ratio
(TFR) of over 3;
(b) if so, the details of total fertility
ratio, State-wise;
(c) whether Government propose to
pursue proactive measures to control
population in such States; and
(d) if so, the details thereof, especially
the feasibility of implementing two child
norm?

60
Status of IISCO, Burnpur
*200. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:
(a) the latest position of Indian Iron
and Steel Company, Burnpur after taken
over by the Steel Authority of India;
(b) the striking and marked
improvement made after being taken over
in terms of reduction of accumulated loss,
reduction of high cost operation,
modernisation, reduction of large working
force and increase in productivity; and
(c) whether there is any further move
to take over a few loss making plants under
SAIL?

Animal diseases in U.P.
†1264. SHRI UDAY PRATAP
SINGH: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal under
Government's consideration for Central
assistance to check animal diseases in Uttar
Pradesh; and
(b) if so, the reasons for delay in its
implementation and the details of the
proposals received from Uttar Pradesh
Government for financial assistance?
Assistance to Karnataka for control of
pests and diseases
1265. SHRIMATI PREMA CARIAPPA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government of Karnataka
has sent any proposal for financial
assistance for control of pests and diseases
and rejuvenation of coconut palm in
Turuvekere Taluk of Tumkur District;
(b) if so, whether any assistance from
Central Development Board has been given
to Karnataka; and
(c) if not, by when the amount would
be released?
Crop damage due to floods
1266. SHRI K. B. KRISHNA
MURTHY:
SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have made any
assessment of extent of damage to the crops
due to recent floods in the various parts of
the country;
(b) if so, the details in terms of value of
the damaged crops and the area affected,
State-wise;
(c) the manner in which Government
plan to help the affected farmers;
(d) the details of the mechanism for
disbursing the help;
(e) whether Government have a
mechanism to monitor the actual disbursal
of help; and

289
(f) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
MIS expenditure
1267. SHRI YASHWANT SINHA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state the total amount of money
spent on Market Invention Schemes and
market support operations during the years
2002-2003 to 2004-2005, commodity-wise
and year-wise?
Declining livestock
†1268. DR. CHHATTRAPAL SINGH
LODHA:
PROF. R.B.S. VARMA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) the total livestock available in the
country at present;
(b) whether it is a fact that the number
of livestock has been declining for the last
five years in the country;
(c) whether Government are aware of
the involvement of slaughter houses in
slaughtering of  bovine, slaughtering of more
than authorised number of animals as also
the slaughtering of stolen animals; and
(d) the action being taken by
Government with regard to aforementioned
slaughter houses and particularly against
those situated in District Aligarh of Uttar
Pradesh?
ICAR research benefits to farmers
1269. SHRI B. K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the laboratories under the
ICAR have a dismal record of translating
their research/development efforts into real
on-field inputs for the farmers;
(b) whether the ICAR labs have brought
out nearly fourteen new high yielding
varieties of seeds but these have not at all
reached the farmers;
(c) whether the farmers are now relying
more on private sector for their hybrid seed
requirements; and
(d) the reasons for ICAR system, with
huge manpower and infrastructure, failing
to transfer its technology to the farmers?
Agricultural growth
†1270. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that agricultural
growth rate has come down to 1.5 per cent
from its desired target of 4 per cent during
the last three years since the beginning of
the Tenth Five Year Plan;
(b) whether it is a fact that necessary
and required investment has been
constantly decreasing in agricultural sector
since 1980 alongwith critical decrease in
agricultural research; and
(c) if so, the steps taken by Government
to bring desired improvement in agricultural
sector?
Policy for doubling agricultural
production
1271. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a
declining trend in the growth rate of
agriculture and the performance of
agriculture has been disturbing;

(b) whether in such a situation, there is
a policy initiated to double our agricultural
production in ten years; and
(c) if so, the thrust and focus to achieve
this policy initiative in terms of investment
in the entire chain of agricultural activities,
infrastructural development, expansion and
upgradation?
National Farmers Welfare Fund
1272. PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that the farmers have to face quite
often the calamities like floods, droughts,
land slides, etc. and suffer losses running
into billions; and
(b) whether Government would
consider to institute National Farmers
Welfare Fund to ensure that the difficulties
faced by the farmers are warded off?
Caterpillar menace in MP
†1273. SHRI P. K. MAHESHWARI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the action being taken by
Government regarding the use of advanced
techniques in agricultural sector;
(b) whether Madhya Pradesh has
always faced the problem of caterpillars
and if so, what steps have been taken by
Government in order to protect the crop of
soyabean from the menace of caterpillars;
and
(c) the kind of cooperation assured by
the Central Government to the State
Government in this regard?
Development of agriculture within
framework of WTO
†1274. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are formulating
any scheme to develop Indian agriculture
within the framework of World Trade
Organisation;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have also
formulated programmes to provide training,
etc. to the farmers therefor; and
(d) if so, the complete details thereof
and the details of the benefits enjoyed by
the farmers as a result thereof?
Special package for cotton production
1275. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have taken any
decision to provide special package for
cotton production with a view to boost the
production of cotton in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
(c) the extent to which the cotton
producing farmers are likely to be benefited
by this special package; and
(d) the measures taken by Government
to dissuade cotton producing farmers from
taking the extreme step of suicide?

291
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Target for foodgrain production
†1276. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
propose to double the production of
foodgrains in the country by the end of
Eleventh Five Year Plan;
(b) if so, the facts in this regard and the
names of the foodgrains alongwith their
respective targeted production by the end
of the Plan;
(c) whether any annual increase rate has
also been fixed right now in order to achieve
the target of this production; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Assistance to fishermen
1277. SHRI LEKHRAJ BACHANI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of fishermen and the
population with fish as a main food;
(b) the number of fishermen who have
been provided with the modest fishing
equipments;
(c) the number of training programmes
organised to train fishermen; and
(d) the number of beneficiaries from
such programmes?
Development of high yield rice variety
1278. SHRI S. ANBALAGAN: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the UN General Assembly
declared the year 2004 as the International
Year of Rice;
(b) if so, the measures taken by
Government in pursuance thereof and the
results achieved therefrom;
(c) whether any initiatives were made
by the Central Government to invest in
high yield varieties of rice, appropriate
technology for post-harvest and pre-
harvest machines and education of farmers
on modern crop management methods; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
achievements made during each of the last
two years?
Assistance to water scarce States
1279. SHRI T. T. V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that agricultural production is
adversely affected in water scarce States
like Tamil Nadu in case of failure of
monsoon;
(b) whether Government have plan to
help such States tide over this problem so
that national annual crop production is not
affected; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Production of edible oils
1280. SHRI THENNALA G.
BALAKRISHNA PILLAI:
SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the production of edible oil
in the country is going down year after
year;

292
(b) if so, the details of demand and
supply of edible oil in the country during
the last three years, year-wise and State-
wise;
(c) the reasons for fall in the production
of edible oil;
(d) whether it is a fact that the edible oil
output is likely to be hit this year also; and
(e) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to increase the production of edible
oil in the country?
Simplifying deep sea fishing rules
1281. SHRI THENNALA G.
BALAKRISHNA PILLAI: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) the manner in which Government
are going to simplify the deep sea fishing
sector;
(b) whether numerous rules and
regulations have been put in place in the
fishing sector;
(c) the extent to which Government are
aware of the fact that some officials are
periodically harassing the fishery sector
through such rules;
(d) whether any guidelines have been
issued to all concerned to avoid harassment
and harm in the Indian fishery sector; and
(e) the steps proposed to be taken to
sensitize the officials to treat fishery as a
development activity?
Devastation of crops due to
substandard seeds and pesticides
†1282. PROF. R. B. S. VARMA:
SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that farmers are
suffering heavy losses due to devastation
of their crops because of substandard seeds
and pesticides;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action taken by Government in
this regard, so far?
Agricultural production in Nagaland
1283. SHRI T. R. ZELIANG: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) the details of Centrally sponsored
programmes formulated and being
implemented by Government for Nagaland
to increase agricultural production during
the last three years;
(b) whether Government have fixed any
target for increasing the agricultural
production; and
(c) if so, the details of achievements
made in this respect?
Land becoming barren in
Chhattisgarh
1284. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
due to pollution in Chhattisgarh, 50,000
acres of cultivable land in Simaga, Siltara
and Mandir Hasaud has turned into barren
land;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether Government are aware that
recently Indira Gandhi Agriculture
University conducted a survey on this issue,
if so, the details of its recommendations
and how Government are going to
implement them?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

293
Agricultural Universities
1285. SHRI VARINDER SINGH
BAJWA: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) the number of Agricultural
Universities functioning in the country, at
present;
(b) whether Government periodically
review their work to provide benefit to the
poor rural agriculturists; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Coverage area of Bt. Cotton
1286. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY:
SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:
SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India has
now become a major player in the transgenic
crops by achieving coverage area of 50,000
hectares;
(b) whether it is also a fact that India
has hiked its Bt. Cotton coverage area by
400 per cent between 2002-04;
(c) if so, in what way India is planning
to galvanise the global biotech crop market
in the next three years; and
(d) whether a study has been made to
find out the benefits of Bt. Cotton to Indian
farmers, if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Loans and credits for deep sea fishing
1287. SHRI S. M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
propose to help the deep sea fishing
industry;
(b) if so, the details of such plans for
this financial year;
(c) whether any financial assistance in
the form of loans will be given for the
acquisition of trawlers;
(d) if so, the details of such schemes;
(e) to what extent, Government tie up
with any financial institutions to ensure
that soft credit is given to the fishing sector;
and
(f) the details of such schemes being
planned?
Bulk drug pricing
1288. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of
CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the National
Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority has
revised the bulk drug prices in the country,
recently;
(b) if so, the details of the drugs whose
prices have been reduced and the details of
drugs whose prices have been increased; and
(c) to what extent the policy helps in
bringing down the prices of drugs in the
country?
Liquidation of sick industries
1289. SHRI DIPANKAR
MUKHERJEE: Will the Minister of
